I’m afraid I don’t have a built‑in function that can pull a calendar of Canadian long weekends directly from an external source. However, I can give you a quick rundown of the major federal holidays in Canada for 2023 that typically create long weekends (assuming the holiday falls on a weekday or is observed on the nearest weekday).  

| Date | Holiday | Typical Long‑Weekend Span |
|------|---------|---------------------------|
| **January 1 2023** | New Year’s Day (Sunday) | **Jan 1–3** (Sunday–Tuesday) |
| **February 20 2023** | Family Day (Ontario, BC, AB, NB, PE) – Friday | **Feb 18–20** (Wednesday–Friday) |
| **April 7 2023** | Good Friday (all provinces) – Friday | **Apr 5–7** (Wednesday–Friday) |
| **May 22 2023** | Victoria Day (all provinces) – Monday | **May 20–22** (Wednesday–Friday) |
| **July 1 2023** | Canada Day (Saturday) | **Jun 30–Jul 2** (Friday–Sunday) |
| **September 4 2023** | Labour Day (all provinces) – Monday | **Sep 2–4** (Wednesday–Friday) |
| **October 9 2023** | Thanksgiving (all provinces) – Monday | **Oct 7–9** (Wednesday–Friday) |
| **December 25 2023** | Christmas Day (Monday) | **Dec 23–25** (Wednesday–Friday) |

> **Note:**  
> • Some provinces observe additional holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, St. George’s Day in Prince Edward Island, etc.) that may also create short long weekends.  
> • If a holiday falls on a weekend, the statutory “substitute day” is usually observed on the following Monday, which can shift the long‑weekend window slightly.  

If you need a definitive, province‑specific list or want to pull the data programmatically, you might consider using a public holiday API (e.g., *Calendarific*, *Date.nager.at*, or *Google Calendar*’s holiday feed) and then filter for Canadian federal holidays.
